summary.text: Cummins Onan RV generator sets start from a control switch on the generator or a remote panel in the vehicle. The status indicator light flashes during preheat and cranking and stays on once running; each model's fault codes and maintenance schedule are in its Operator Manual.

models.text: Each Cummins Onan generator set has a spec number description, shown on the serial number tag attached to the generator.
Current gasoline sets: QG 4000i (HGLBA), QG 5500/7000 EFI (HGJAA, HGJAD), QG 5500/7000 (HGJAB, HGJAE) and QG 7000iDF. Cummins uses HGJAx to mean HGJAA, HGJAB, HGJAD and HGJAE.
Gasoline/LP sets: QG 2800i/2500i LP (HGLAA), QG 4000/3600 LP (KYFA) and QG 5500/6500 LP (HGJAB, HGJAE).
Diesel sets: QD 3200 (HDZAA), QD 6000 (HDKAH, HDKAV), QD 8000 (HDKAK), QD 10,000 (HDKCA, HDKCC) and QD 12500 (HDKCB, HDKAW).

EC-AGS+ works with Quiet Diesel HDKA, HDKB and HDKC (kit A065U740) and gas/LPG HGJBB, HGLAA, HGJAA, HGJAB, HGJAD, HGJAE and KY (kit A065U664). On discontinued HDCAA, HDCAB, KV and KVD, displayed fault codes are not accurate.
The Energy Command 30 lists KV and KVD MicroLite/CampPower 2.8/2.5 kW sets as models without a status light that do not support diagnostic fault codes.

display.text: While starting, the status indicator flashes during preheat and cranking; preheat can take up to 15 seconds before cranking begins. The indicator stays on continuously when the starter disconnects and the set is running.
When priming, the status indicator light stays on solid while the fuel pump runs.
On an Energy Command 30 panel, the START/STOP switch has a red backlight while the genset runs. On sets with diagnostics it flashes the fault and decodes it into a text fault message.
EC-30 SERVICE IN counts down to the next service; when it elapses the display alternates SERVICE DUE and ENTER to Reset. Press STOP three times to display the last fault message.
EC-30 SYSTEM INFO shows the reason for the last automatic action, such as AUTO RUN LOW BAT (started because the battery was low) or AUTO STOP NO SAFETY (no safety input sensed for 30 days).

The EC-AGS+ app Alerts screen shows maintenance and exercise reminders, firmware updates and gateway accelerometer faults. Generator fault codes shown in the app are generator issues, not EC-AGS+ hardware or app issues.

reset.text: Excessive cranking can overheat the starter. If the set does not start within the set time it stops cranking automatically; wait at least 2 minutes before trying again, then use the Operator Manual troubleshooting.
The generator keeps running after a circuit breaker trips. Turn off as many loads as possible, push the breaker to OFF to reset it, then ON to reconnect the circuit.
EC-30: after servicing, go to SERVICE DUE and press ENTER to reset the service hour-meter. If serviced early, go to SERVICE IN, press SET, then ENTER.
EC-30: whenever the safety input changes (ignition, brake or park), the genset stops and the mode changes to MANUAL. After parking in a safe location, press AUTO GEN, then ENTER to confirm AUTO ON.

EC-30: if the safety input has not changed for 25 days the display flashes SAFETY OFF & ON; switch the ignition, transmission position or brake to reset the 30-day timer. At day 30 AUTO GEN is disabled.
EC-AGS+: a significant vehicle acceleration disables AGS, AGS is disabled after 30 days in AGS, and operating a generator or remote start/stop switch manually also disables AGS.

checks.text: Pre-start checks: make sure all vehicle CO detectors work, check for fuel and exhaust leaks and exhaust damage, make sure curbs or logs are not reducing ground clearance, turn off air conditioners and large appliances, and check oil.

Before the first start of the day and every eight hours, check oil level, coolant (if equipped), fuel line fittings, battery terminals, mounting bolts, and that the air inlet and outlet are not blocked.
If the set ran out of fuel, prime it: hold the control switch at STOP/PRIME for at least 30 seconds on gasoline sets and 1 minute on diesel sets.

Power drops about 3.5% of rated power per 1000 ft (305 m) of elevation; run fewer appliances at altitude. In cold weather, check the altitude setting if equipped and that fuel and oil suit the temperature.
checks.locator: 'Power vs. Altitude' and 'Operating in Cold Weather' (PDF p. 1)

checks.text: Cummins recommends a 600 cold cranking amp starting battery and at least 12 inches (305 mm) of ground clearance; loose or corroded battery connections make starting harder.

EC-AGS+ will not start in Auto: start with the local generator control switch and read its fault code, check for an Accelerometer Fault alert, then check temperature, Quiet Time, phone clock and house battery start settings.
EC-AGS+ will not run the A/C: check the temperature setting, the temperature sensor coin cell battery, Bluetooth range between sensor and gateway, Quiet Time settings, and gateway battery voltage.
Automatic starting is not allowed with the house battery below 9 volts. In auto mode the set runs at least 10 minutes, and starts two hours before Quiet Time if the batteries are not full.
If an EC-30 controller misbehaves, first check whether the genset runs correctly from its own controls; if not, the problem is in the genset, not the EC-30.
For storage, Cummins offers OnaFresh GXLP Fuel Stabilizer (part 326-5365; 16 oz treats 40 gallons of gasoline) and Onagard Storage Fogging Spray (part 326-5288) for up to six months of storage.

parts.text: The muffler is mounted inside the generator housing and has a USDA Forest Service spark arrestor. Replace the pressure cap (if equipped) every two years.
The EC-AGS+ kit contains a gateway, temperature sensor, power harness and Y-harness. Do not install the gateway directly in the generator set compartment.
If the EC-AGS+ app shows an Accelerometer Fault, Auto mode cannot be engaged; the manual's corrective action is to replace the gateway.
The EC-30 needs a safety signal input from the vehicle ignition, the brake light (trailers, fifth wheels, campers) or air brake on diesel motorhomes, or the park/neutral signal.

callTech.text: Minor coolant leaks can be topped up at the recovery tank but should be serviced by a qualified technician as soon as possible; larger leaks mean shutting the set down until it is serviced.
If an exhaust leak is found, shut the generator set down and have it serviced before running it. If fuel, oil or exhaust leaks appear after starting, stop it immediately and have it serviced.
If a circuit breaker trips again right away, the appliance has a short or the breaker is faulty: call a qualified technician.
Never run the set in a garage or confined space, and never occupy the vehicle while it runs without CO detectors. Disable automatic starting before storing or parking in a garage.

Always disable AGS before sleeping without a working CO detector, garaging, storing, fueling, or servicing the genset, batteries or appliances; disconnect the battery or genset remote harness to disable it.
Cummins recommends EC-30 START/STOP voltage settings be changed only by qualified personnel who understand the charging system and have checked its operating voltages.
